result.title: ESSI: Computationally Efficient Semantic Search for Sparse Autoencoder Concepts
result.summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) decompose diffusion model activations into interpretable features, but steering a model with them requires identifying which features map to a given semantic concept, if any. Existing methods for this concept to feature task are expensive, relying on grid searches or repeated passes through the frozen UNet. We propose Efficient Semantic Sparse Identification (ESSI). Using segmentation masks to label SDXL activations as concept or non-concept, ESSI ranks SAE features and binary-searches for the smallest set on which a linear classifier still separates positive from negative samples while not falling below a performance threshold, then reuses that classifier to calibrate the steering strength. We evaluate the same selected features on both concept insertion and object unlearning. Compared with prior work, ESSI is as cheap or cheaper, and performs well on both insertion and removal.

AI.brief_summary: ESSI 面向扩散模型 SAE 特征定位，用分割掩码标注 SDXL 激活，对 SAE 特征排序并二分搜索仍可线性分离概念的最小特征集，再复用该分类器校准 steering 强度，并在概念插入与物体遗忘上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「概念到特征」的搜索与最小充分特征集验证，可能为 LVR 中 latent 假设筛选和视觉证据选择提供方法线索；但研究对象是图像生成 steering 而非推理状态，线性可分判据能否迁移尚需核查。
